description:
A space for space enthusiasts and story tellers.

Team members should have a zeal for space exploration and story telling.
summary:
Space Ghosts (Echoes of the Moon) is an immersive educational platform developed to bring abandoned NASA hardware back to life.
What we developed: A digital storytelling experience centered on three iconic artifacts—the Opportunity Mars rover, the Apollo 11 Eagle lunar module, and the Ingenuity Mars helicopter.
How it addresses the challenge: Inspired by traditional storytelling that honors guardians, our project reframes retired machinery as "Space Ghosts." It bridges the gap between dense technical archives and youth (ages 9–26) by pairing rigorous NASA telemetry with emotional 3D-styled narratives. Furthermore, it connects historical engineering to modern youth technology, showing how Opportunity's navigation powers mobile AR apps, Apollo underpins mobile computing, and Ingenuity drives consumer drones.
Why it is important: Grounded in a childhood journey of staring at the stars in Uganda, Space Ghosts turns dry historical data into an inspiring bridge from dreams to global science.
details:
The Concept: Space Ghosts is an immersive, narrative-driven educational tool designed to bring retired and abandoned NASA hardware back to life. Instead of leaving historical spacecraft buried in dense technical archives, our project transforms them into "silent guardians" of the cosmos.

How It Works: We focus on three iconic off-world artifacts: Opportunity (the Mars rover that walked the red dust for nearly 15 years), Eagle (the Apollo 11 lunar module whose descent stage remains permanently at the Sea of Tranquility), and Ingenuity (the tiny 1.8 kg helicopter that achieved 72 powered flights on Mars). The platform weaves authentic mission data, coordinates, and telemetry into emotional, storytelling-led experiences that guide users through their historic journeys, discoveries, and final resting places.

Bridging the Curiosity Gap: Traditional history and space archives can be dry and difficult for casual learners to navigate. Space Ghosts makes space exploration deeply relatable, emotional, and accessible.

Connecting Past to Present: It explicitly demonstrates how historical engineering foundations directly power modern youth technology—connecting Opportunity’s autonomous navigation to mobile AR mapping apps, Apollo’s telemetry to cloud-connected mobile UIs, and Ingenuity’s carbon-fiber rotor blades to high-performance consumer FPV drones.

Target Audience (Ages 9 to 26): Built for digital natives, students, and young space enthusiasts worldwide who look up at the night sky or experience space primarily through movies and mobile apps.

Global & Local Inspiration: Initiated from Kampala, Uganda, this project proves that a passion for space exploration and open science transcends borders. As a child staring at the stars in Uganda, our team lead dreamed of touching the cosmos through stargazing apps and films; Space Ghosts is designed to be that exact bridge for the next generation of global dreamers, sparking a lifelong curiosity for science, engineering, and astronomy

Design & Prototyping: Canva and PowerPoint for designing interactive presentation layouts, 3D visual concept mock ups, and dynamic user interfaces.

 

Data Sources & Research: Official NASA archives and datasets, including the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), Mars Exploration Rover telemetry, Apollo 11 landing site summaries and seismic/sample records (21.5 kg), and Ingenuity flight log and mishap archives.

 

The "Space Ghosts" Folklore Narrative: Drawing inspiration from traditional cultural storytelling where elders and ancestors who came before us leave behind a lasting legacy of guidance, we re-framed retired hardware not as "space junk," but as spiritual sentinels guarding alien worlds.

Immersive Visual Design: We integrated 3D-styled animated concept visuals, holographic data nodes, and vibrant digital storyboards to capture the imagination of young digital natives.

Scientific Validity vs. Narrative Engagement: We ensured that every piece of folklore and storytelling is strictly backed by rigorous, authentic NASA mission data.

Accessibility & Age Appropriateness: We evaluated how young learners (ages 9–26) consume information, designing an experience that bridges the gap between complex engineering telemetry and emotional, human-centred storytelling.
